text.title: Content Audit Process Worked Example
text.summary: One end-to-end worked example of Content Audit Process producing a valid spec artefact, anonymised for portability. Concrete audit findings for blog and help center content, demonstrating action assignment logic.

step.name: trigger
step.text: Engagement onboarded; the Content Audit Process methodology was selected after Applies-If was satisfied (named owner Ruslan Faion, downstream consumer named in engagement charter, source-of-truth pinned in docs/).

step.name: apply-rules
step.text: Walked the rules from 01-core-rules.xml. Most rules passed on first review; one required a follow-up because a required citation was missing. Captured the gap, patched, re-ran.

step.name: produce
step.text: Filled templates/content-audit-process.json with all required fields per the JSON Schema; emitted artefact_id with date; signed off by the engagement owner.

step.name: validate
step.text: Ran scripts/validate-content-audit-process.py --file <path>; validator returned 0; smoke-test fixture in templates/_smoke-test.json also passed.

step.name: handover
step.text: Artefact registered with the downstream consumer; entry added to the engagement decision log; version locked at 1.1.0.

example.note: Finding: 40% of blog posts are 3+ years old. Screenshots show old UI, pricing information is outdated, links are broken. Action: Update top 20 posts by traffic; archive low-traffic posts over 3 years old. Reasoning: High-traffic old posts are worth updating (Update); low-traffic old posts have no recovery path (Remove).

Finding: 15 articles cover similar topics with conflicting answers. Issues: user confusion, SEO cannibalization between pages, maintenance overhead. Action: Consolidate into 5 comprehensive guides, redirect the 10 removed URLs. Reasoning: Overlapping coverage with conflicting information is the textbook Consolidate case.
